reviews.author: Youngmi Choi
reviews.text:
The moment you enter **Hyundai Department Store (The Hyundai Seoul)** in Yeouido, you immediately feel that this is not just a ‘shopping space’. As soon as you walk through the door, what fills your view is the beauty of the space itself rather than the products. The atrium structure with a long opening above gives the impression of entering a huge art museum, and the curved balconies connected on each floor create a gentle rhythm. This architecture, which chose curves rather than straight lines, naturally draws people's gaze upward and to the side, giving the gift of relaxation just by walking.
The lighting pouring from the ceiling is not excessive. Round-shaped lights are placed at regular intervals to subtly surround the entire space. The light reflects off the marble floor, creating a luxurious scene both during the day and at night. The stipple-like twinkle of the lights forming on the floor is as delicate as starlight. So here, rather than hastening our steps, we naturally slow down.
Even the space lined with luxury stores feels refined rather than overwhelming. The boundaries between brands are clear, but not stuffy, and the display visible beyond the show window is structured like an exhibition. It is impressive that names such as Louis Vuitton and Prada blend into the space and exist in ‘harmony’ rather than ‘show-off’. The reason why I want to take a picture every time I pass by the store is because of that sense of balance.
The real charm of The Hyundai Seoul is that it brings nature indoors. The green space spread out in the middle of the room makes you forget for a moment that it is a department store. The garden, with trees, plants, dirt paths, and wooden decks, is like a greenhouse in the city. As you walk along the trail among the plants, you first get the sense of ‘taking a break’ rather than the purpose of shopping. Everyone, from children to adults, naturally stops in front of this space.
A different atmosphere unfolds in the lighting store or lifestyle zone. The scenery with lights of different designs on does not feel stuffy at all even under the low ceiling, but rather creates a cozy and sensuous mood. Even each chair and table are carefully arranged, making the entire space feel like a curation.
Even on weekends when a lot of people come and go, this place strangely doesn't feel crowded. This is thanks to the wide movement path, open view, and blank spaces provided here and there. So, The Hyundai Seoul is not a ‘department store where you go to shop’, but is more like a place where you go to spend the day. The whole process of walking slowly, looking, resting, and walking again is natural.
You can find such a sophisticated yet comfortable space in the middle of Yeouido. The Hyundai Seoul has clearly changed the cityscape. The time spent here remains as an experience, not a consumption, and the sensitivity of the space is fully captured in each photo. That's why I keep coming back, and when the seasons change, I want to see different faces.
Yeouido Hyundai Department Store is already a cityscape in itself.

reviews.text:
"It's nice that it's big and spacious, but it's disappointing that the space utilization seems monotonous."

While looking around, someone behind me said to his group, "I wonder if it's true that I ran for two hours just to see this."

There is a large space in the center, a corridor-style corridor surrounding it, and a store is located between the corridor and the outer wall of the building. This is a grammar we have become so familiar with that it is almost boring.

The difference is that it is indoors, but what architectural engineering technology is needed to create such a space indoors and what kind of design should be designed to maximize it are issues that architects and construction companies should have been concerned about.

If so, the department store should have thought about how to secure the differentiation of the space or program as the environment is controlled, assuming that this is implemented, but it seems that there was laziness in this regard.

Just as Shinsegae Group's Starfield series introduced various spatial compositions based on books and programs that fit them, it was an opportunity to create Hyundai's own popular and productive culture and expand it into the group's identity, but it seems to have been blown away. As an observer, I am disappointed. I hope that Hyundai Department Store, the party involved, will feel the greatest regret and continue to think about it.

reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Yeonhui-dong #Pyeonganru #Start in 2025

“American Cantonese cuisine in Korea”
“A house where you can taste as much as you know”
“Happy New Year”

Many people know that there are many good Chinese restaurants in Yeonhui-dong, but many good classic Chinese restaurants have closed and it feels like the movies are gradually losing their luster.
In the meantime, I came across a place where I could check out the spectrum of Chinese food in Yeonhui-dong, and that is it.

Cantonese restaurants in the U.S. do seafood quite well.
The restaurants in LA that we have already introduced are representative examples, and this restaurant also has the DNA of American-style Cantonese cuisine while embodying the unique taste of Pyeonganlu.
The Taiwanese owner, who has been running a Cantonese restaurant in the United States for about 30 years, is very proud of his cooking, as if he is still doing his own thing in Korea.

#cold vegetables
It’s a fairly unique cold dish.
What makes it different from others is that it contains braised pork ribs.
The ribs are lightly braised in soy sauce, and although they are a bit dry, they are not a bad choice as a cold dish.
Another feature of this restaurant is that the cold jellyfish salad also includes cabbage.
Five-spice soybean pork is ordinary.

#Yoringgi
The most unique dish among the dishes in this house is Yuringi.
It doesn't feel like a normal period of violation in our country.
First of all, when a whole chicken is fried, it feels like you are receiving a wonderful whole chicken dish.
In addition, the batter is thin, so it is completely different from the existing Yuringi.
The acidic soy sauce and red peppers are typical of Yuringi, but pouring hot oil over them to make it Chinese-style is also unique to this restaurant.
There is no other place like this unique violation except this house.

#Fried dumplings
I knew this place made their own dumplings and I heard they were delicious, but the dumplings on this day were disappointing.
The fried dumplings were fried well, but the dumpling skin had an unpleasant floury smell, probably because it wasn't ripe enough.
Instead, light beef is good.

#stir-fried clams
Stir-fried clams are served at a Chinese restaurant.
Usually, it is made with clams, but here it is made with lilies, so it has a richer taste and makes eating clams even more fun.
It has a slightly spicy taste and is thickened by adding starch.
This sauce later turns into a finishing meal.

#red pepper shrimp
You told me the name of this dish, which is an authentic Taiwanese dish, but I forgot the name, so I'll order it red pepper shrimp.
I split the jalapenos, added the shrimp balls, fried them, and then stir-fried them with kkanpung sauce.
This is quite a delicacy. It's a method that requires a lot of work, but I highly recommend it because it's a delicious accompaniment to alcohol.
They say that this day was the last time they ate it because the jalapeño season was over.
Let’s aim for next season.

#Stir-fried crab
Highlight stir-fried crab.
A time-consuming dish made by frying female crabs and then sautéing them in soy sauce.
Although the flavors of soy sauce and oyster sauce are dominant, the flavor of the crab overcomes them, making this an excellent crab dish.
The taste of scraping off crab shells is also great.

#Steamed rockfish
They make Chinese-style steamed rockfish properly.
The rockfish is steamed, sprinkled with soy sauce and poured with oil to give it a nutty flavor, and a lot of coriander is added to enhance the flavor.
Among the steamed rockfish dishes I've eaten these days, this is one of the most delicious dishes.

#clam pasta
The finishing dish served as clam pasta was stir-fried clam noodles in stir-fried clam sauce.
This is also really delicious as a finishing touch. Has vongole ever failed?
I don’t think there’s any ending quite like this in Chinese food.

#Sweet pumpkin soup
For dessert, sweet and sour pumpkin is served.
Fried sweet pumpkin and finished with sweet and sour sauce.
However, it is a little sweeter than regular sweet and sour sauce.
As a dessert, the sweetness is acceptable.

#drink
The finishing drink is also a traditional Taiwanese drink, which is a savory and sweet drink made with mung beans, coconut, and rock sugar.
The combination of savory and clean taste is good.
This is also my first time trying this.

#Comprehensive
This style of cooking is hard to find in Korea.
Yeonhui-dong also has an overwhelming uniqueness.
The taste is unique and the style is good.
Instead, it is sweet overall.
People who are sensitive to sweet taste may be overtaken by the sweet taste if they eat this many courses.
There is enough saltiness to counteract this.
Although the strong taste sticks to your mouth, it is not the same flavor that competes with the mildness of the ingredients like authentic Cantonese cuisine.
I think this appearance may be a slightly modified version of the Korean style.

PS: This is a restaurant where people have different tastes as much as they know about it and have experience with it.
Experience with Cantonese cuisine,
American Chinese food experience,
Experience with American-style Cantonese cuisine,
Experience with Korean Chinese food,
I think that all of these experiences will determine whether you like or dislike the taste.

It's been a while since I saved this store because I thought it looked good after seeing it in Yeonggu Bread's review and wanted to go there, but like the nearby Yeonhui Restaurant that I stopped by last time, it didn't seem like the food was served in small sizes with the feel of a drink menu, so I tried to stop by with my family, but since I rarely leave the neighborhood, I was just stamping my feet, so I finally decided to go today, and stopped by shortly after the store's opening time for the evening.

When I got to the store, I realized that it was close to Heege, which I stopped by last time, and that I also stopped by Yeonhui Restaurant recently, but before that, it was my first visit in a long time since I went to Chinese restaurants in Yeonnam-dong and Yeonhui-dong a long time ago.

I knew about the availability of parking at the store because I had previously inquired over the phone. I was about to call to inquire about where I should park, but the clerk came out of the store and showed me where to park, so I parked and went into the store. He said that all the family members sitting by the window had reserved seats except for this table. When I looked around, almost every empty table except ours was set up, so I guess it was popular and my expectations rose.

I roughly knew the menu, and since we have a young family, we mainly order familiar and common dishes. First, sweet and sour pork for the young family, Nanja Wansu, which is the menu item that made us want to come to this house, and since the family members don't like greasy food very much, we want to order Jjamppong, but we choose between the special seafood Jjamppong, called red Jjamppong, and the pork belly Jjamppong, called white Jjamppong. I ordered pork belly jjamppong and asked for a beer.

First, they set out salty jachai, pickled radish, and Chinese kimchi, and there was a pitcher of cold water on the table. The aunt at the table next to me brought a glass pitcher that looked like jasmine tea, so I asked for jasmine tea, and she also brought a glass pitcher filled with warm jasmine tea.

When I looked around the store, it seemed like it was a new store in a new building, so it didn't feel like a Chinese restaurant, but it had a pleasant feel. Chinese-style decorations like carp decorations hanging here and there showed that it was a Chinese restaurant.

After waiting a bit, the egg cups I was looking forward to came out first. Looking at the photos, it felt like it had quite a good volume, but in reality, the overall volume felt a bit disappointing, perhaps because the plate itself was a bit small in size. The color was not the darker brown color I had in mind, and the thickness of the egg cups seemed a bit thin, so my first impression was a bit disappointing.

I almost always eat nanjawans with a sauce made with soy sauce, a lot of vinegar, and plenty of chili oil, so I asked for chili oil, so they brought it to me. After making the soy sauce, I was excited to see what it would taste like. I took a bite and tasted it before dipping it in the soy sauce. I guess they finished it with sesame oil at the end of cooking. I could sense the scent of sesame oil, and the nanja pork belly had almost no odor and felt like it was just made with pork. It's thick enough that you can eat it without any soy sauce, but it doesn't feel special.

Dipping it in soy sauce adds a subtle spiciness from the chili oil, making it quite good.

Sweet and sour pork came out soon after, and the sauce wasn't packaged separately, so why didn't it come out separately? The young family members also said they wanted to pour in the sauce and tasted it. The batter was fluffy and the meat was lean, so it wasn't tough or had any odor, so it felt safe to eat. The sweet and sour pork's sauce wasn't too sweet, but it had a slightly sweet taste, so it would have been better if it was a little less sweet, but the young family members liked it because it was delicious.The pork belly jjamppong was also served, and when I tasted it, the pork belly was sliced relatively thinly, lightly fried, and placed on top of the jjamppong. Although I am now somewhat accustomed to pork, it still takes a bit of courage to eat food with soup and something with a strong pork flavor, like pork belly, rather than the chashu of Japanese ramen. So I took a deep breath and tasted it. The soup was thick, but clear, rather than thick. It's nice that the Cheongyang peppers are finely chopped and it feels spicy and freshly cooked, but I still don't think the pork belly tastes better.

The sweet and sour pork also felt a bit disappointing in terms of volume, but my young family member wanted to eat it all by herself, so I ordered shrimp with chili, another classic menu item that I was curious about. I asked if I could order another sweet and sour pork in case the younger family member wanted to eat more, and the family member said that they should order egg fried rice instead of sweet and sour pork. The young family member agreed and asked for egg fried rice as well. Overall, I felt that the volume of the food in this house was a bit disappointing. Please give me a generous amount of egg fried rice.

I tend to like fried rice, and I like Mapo Oebaek's fried rice, but I haven't yet found fried rice that I like. I actually like chahang, a simple Japanese fried rice served at Japanese ramen shops, and I was wondering if this restaurant's simple egg fried rice would be good, so I thought it was good.

After waiting a little longer, the chili shrimp finally came out. As described, the shrimp were quite large, so it felt like good value for money. When I tasted it, it was medium shrimp, so the overall volume of the dish wasn't great, but the shrimp themselves had a good volume and the taste was very familiar with chili shrimp, and it was still a bit rich, just like I experienced in the food at this house, so it felt like I was eating it with more of a sauce flavor rather than the scent of the shrimp or something like that.

Lastly, the egg fried rice was served with egg soup. When I took a bite, I could feel the scent of sesame oil, but the taste itself was not that special that I had come to expect. It felt like fried rice from a typical Chinese restaurant in Korea. It was a bit funny that a young family member was looking for Jjajang sauce and tried to eat it with Jjajang sauce even though they were young. When I asked the clerk, he said that Jjajang sauce is not served with egg fried rice, but I guess I don't like eating it with Jjajang sauce. When I told my young family that it would taste better just eating it, they seemed to want to eat it with Jjajang sauce, and the clerk brought me some leftover stir-fried Jjajang sauce, so my young family ate it well with Jjajang sauce, but when I tasted it too, I didn't think it was a vegetable-based Jjajang sauce.

There was some leftover egg fried rice and chili-stuffed shrimp, so I asked them to take it out, but I felt like my stomach was going to explode, so I decided to walk a bit.

It seemed to be a store that serves egg shank, which is hard to find these days, and it looked pretty good, so I decided to stop by, and what I felt about the overall cuisine was that it reminded me of the dishes I had at various Gangnam Chinese restaurants that I always went to when I ate out at my house when I was young. Just like I felt at Gadam in Apgujeong before, it felt like Chinese food with a taste that I was very familiar with since I was young, so I didn't feel the original feel of this restaurant, and the seasoning was a bit thick, although it wasn't tasteless, but it was less good than expected. I think this place probably tastes better with five-spice beef or five-spice chicken, so if I stop by again, I'll try those menu items.

reviews.author: kiri go
reviews.text:
I suddenly feel like I can't keep up with trends. To give you a mental victory, I am now at an age where I am not sensitive to trends. For example, interest in vegan food has increased recently, but it is separate from the trend. It's just because digestion power is poor. I am looking for vegetarian options that I can accept without burden. The only thing we are familiar with in our daily lives are vegetables. So these days, I only eat vegetables, almost like people from an island. His nickname is Namulman. Even when delivering parcels, write Namulman in the recipient field.

While I was there, I saw that Bezzies had opened on Hongyeon-gil. The location is across from Yonsei Mart. I had never been to a restaurant with a baby before, but it happened to be a non-discriminatory store with a ramp for the door, and when I looked for it, I was told that they also had highchairs for children, which gave me courage. Even though I had to wait like a ninja for when my child was sleeping and put him in a baby carrier, I felt at ease knowing that he was welcome. I learned that kindness should not be taken for granted. I sat down at the table with gratitude.

To be really honest, I visited it thinking it would be a hip place. It's a trait that can't keep up with trends, but I'm curious about what young people like these days. I'm not sensitive to trends. It's like having a crush on trends or something like that.

I don't know much about hips, but I could tell that the store was overall clean and warm. I liked the cotton fabrics that carefully covered something. I could feel the desire to make sure that even the smallest details were not intrusive. In particular, the white linen cloth that was lightly attached to the window and made the inside of the store feel cozy was stunning. I liked that loose consideration. The vegetable props used throughout the store were also cute. The eggplant model holding down a tissue and the mushroom on the bathroom key made me smile.

The menu here is all vegan. Additionally, it is diverse. As the name of the store suggests. Pasta, gnocchi, taco rice, salad, sandwich, burger, toast, grilled food and even soup. It was like, ‘I didn’t know what your taste would be, so I prepared everything!’ Nevertheless, each dish had its own presence. This is the Girls’ Generation of the vegan restaurant world. It's Super Junior.
Being the man I am, I chose ‘Leek Pesto Pasta and Bracken Bracken’. My wife, who is studying Spanish, ordered ‘Mexican Taco Rice.’ We were satisfied because we could each eat the food we wanted. We also added today's soup, which we both like. For drinks, I chose grapefruit ade and soy milk highball. Because highballs are trendy these days.

It was delicious. Even if you ask how it can be expressed so simply, I can only answer that it doesn't require any special formulas. It's a pity that I can only say that something delicious is delicious, but I can't help it because it was literally delicious. Detailed taste descriptions can be listed. However, rather than saying that each individual flavor was strong, I would like to emphatically say that it was simply delicious because the combined flavors on the plate were delicious overall without any awkwardness.

Sometimes, when you look closely at trends, it feels like they are a bit violent. This is because trends are somewhat forced upon us. To be honest, the vegan trend was like that to me. As someone who has enjoyed delicious meat for decades, I have felt an uncomfortable sense of guilt. Occasionally, I have encountered messages containing criticism. Vegetarianism was quite hip, so I felt like I was unenlightened if I didn't enjoy it. ‘It’s not good to eat meat’. After listening, I nodded and tried to clear my mind for a few days, but in the end, it was difficult to overcome the thought that ‘meat is delicious’ that was deeply programmed in my head. Fads are usually short-lived. To me, the vegan message was more of a trend.

But the food at Bezis was delicious enough. Even if I ate only vegetarian food, my hunger was satisfied. The realization that it was not a life of Buddhist abstinence and that it would be okay to continue eating like this crept into me. It moved my heart more than any other vegan message I had experienced. My thoughts changed. Yes, let’s enjoy delicious vegetables. In order to do that, a vegan restaurant called Veggies must remain open for a long time. I hope it doesn't become hip like a trend. I hope it will continue to be remembered as a restaurant of just one genre, like a Chinese restaurant or a Japanese restaurant. First of all, I'll have to visit again when my baby can eat today's soup with me.

goûtmontée: It is said to mean ‘a combination of flavors and textures’ in French.

This place specializes in desserts made with feuilletage dough, which is a layer of thin dough. There are also tarts, but people seem to have different preferences compared to feuitage, so I ordered Saint-Honoré and Pralinette.

♤ Saint-Honoré (9,200₩)
It is a different style from the typical Saint-Honoré, but it has caramel and vanilla cream in between the feuillet, and is finished with a small caramel choux on top. It was an impressive dessert in both texture and taste, with the extremely crunchy and sweet feuuitage, the thick cream in between, and the crunchy choux. I could understand why many people gave it favorable reviews.

♤ Pralinette (9,500₩)
Similarly, the space between the feuillets was filled with nut cream, caramel, and nuts coated in caramel with praline. It is much crispier, more savory, and sweeter than Saint-Honoré. Because it is a dessert with such a strong taste, it is more memorable. However, if you eat this first, the taste of other menu items may be overshadowed, so it is recommended to eat it later.

It was the most eye-opening dessert I've had in a long time. I want to visit again next time and try other menus.

If you want to taste authentic European sourdough bread in Seoul, be sure to visit Siebel Bakery. This place has it all: delicious bread, a cozy space, friendly staff, and even a dog-friendly atmosphere.

I was looking for delicious bread in Korea because I missed the high-quality sourdough bread commonly found in Europe, and I was really happy to find Ziebel Bakery. It was beyond my expectations.

Above all, I was really impressed by the staff. He spoke fluent English, was friendly, and communicated well. The store was small, but cozy and bright, and even allowed dogs, which made it even more attractive. The menu is simple and focused on sourdough, which I liked.

Before writing this, I visited a few times to make sure the bread was always delicious. I tried the rye bread and it was fantastic. It had a rich and chewy texture, just like the bread I enjoyed eating in Europe. This was my favorite bread. I tried ciabatta, focaccia, and plain sourdough bread, and they were all excellent quality. The biggest compliment I can give is that the bread here is on par with famous bakeries in Europe :)

I also tried the coffee and it was really delicious. The staff are true sourdough experts and were happy to talk about their bread making process and experiments. Since it is a new bakery and is still innovating, the menu may change over time.

If you are looking for authentic, high-quality sourdough bread in Seoul, give Zibel a try. You will never regret it!
